chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him say: 'Any woman who is divorced, then her husband dies before her waiting period (iddah) expires, and she has not become prohibited to him, then she inherits him. She observes the waiting period of the one whose husband died. And if she dies while in her waiting period and has not become prohibited to him, then he inherits her.' And if the woman whose husband died is pregnant, then her waiting period is the further of the two periods: if four months and ten days pass and she has not given birth, then her waiting period is until she gives birth. And if she gives birth before the expiration of four months and ten days, then the waiting period upon her is four months and ten days. This was narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and inheritance status of a divorced woman if her husband dies before the divorce is finalized?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the legal status of a woman in the 'waiting period of revocable divorce' (Iddah al-Talaq) upon her husband's death, establishing that she inherits him as a widow and observes the widow's waiting period (Iddah al-Widowhood). It further resolves the potential conflict between the fixed period of four months and ten days and the duration of pregnancy by applying the principle of observing the longer duration, a key jurisprudential ruling in Shia fiqh. This highlights the precision of Imami jurisprudence in handling overlapping legal conditions regarding inheritance and marital status.
